# markermd

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/rundel/markermd/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/rundel/markermd/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![pkgdown](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-pkgdown-blue.svg)](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/)

markermd is a Shiny-based grading environment for assignments submitted
as git repositories containing Quarto (`.qmd`) documents, such as the
classroom layouts produced by
[ghclass](https://rundel.github.io/ghclass/)’s `org_grade_assignment()`.
Each submission is parsed into a document tree (via
[q2r](https://github.com/rundel/q2r)), validated against the structural
requirements of the assignment, and graded question by question with a
fast, hotkey-driven rubric interface. The template, the rubric, and all
recorded grading live in a per-project SQLite database.

R Markdown (`.Rmd`) assignments are also supported: pass
`use_qmd = FALSE` to
[`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md).

The package is built around two apps:

- [`template()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template.md)
  authors a grading template: which document sections are the questions,
  and what structural rules each answer must satisfy.
- [`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md) grades
  a collection of student repositories against that template with
  per-question rubrics.

Around the apps, a set of helper functions makes the entire workflow
scriptable (see [Scripting the workflow](#scripting-the-workflow)), and
bundled agent skills for Claude Code and Codex can scaffold the template
and rubric, repair submissions the strict parser rejects, or apply the
rubric across all submissions as a first pass for human review (see
[Agent skills](#agent-skills-claude-code-and-codex)).

## Experimental status

This package is experimental: APIs may change significantly and some
features are incomplete.

This project is also an ongoing experiment in “vibe” coding with Claude
Code. Not all implementation details have been thoroughly evaluated, and
there is a lot of wonkiness throughout the codebase.

## Installation

Install the development version of markermd from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rundel/markermd")

# Or using remotes
remotes::install_github("rundel/markermd")
```

### Dependencies

markermd relies on [q2r](https://github.com/rundel/q2r) for parsing
Quarto documents. q2r wraps the Quarto parser via Rust, so installing it
requires a Rust toolchain (`rustc >= 1.85`):

``` r

remotes::install_github("rundel/q2r")
```

## Quick start

A markermd project is a directory containing the student repositories
and, optionally, a solution (key) repository and rendered reports:

    hw01/
    ├── repos/
    │   ├── student1-hw01/
    │   │   └── assignment.qmd
    │   ├── student2-hw01/
    │   └── ...
    ├── html/              # rendered reports, shown while grading
    └── hw01-key/          # solution repository (optional)

``` r

library(markermd)

# One-time setup: writes .markermd/config.yml, creates the grading
# database, installs the bundled agent skills, and writes CLAUDE.md /
# AGENTS.md project instructions for them
init_project("hw01")

# Author the grading template (questions + validation rules)
template("hw01")

# Grade the student repositories
mark("hw01")
```

[`init_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/init_project.md)
detects the key repository and the artifact directories (the directories
of rendered reports), records everything in `hw01/.markermd/config.yml`,
and creates the SQLite database that stores the template, the rubric,
and all grading.

[`project_sitrep()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/project_sitrep.md)
prints an overview of a project’s configuration at any point, and
[`project_set()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/project_set.md)
changes it, including the artifact directories (`artifacts =`).
Re-running
[`init_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/init_project.md)
keeps the configured artifact directories rather than adding every new
top-level folder; `rescan_artifacts = TRUE` rebuilds the list.

## Template creation with `template()`

The template app loads an assignment and displays its structure as an
interactive tree. The assignment can be a project’s key repository, a
single `.qmd` / `.Rmd` file or a directory containing one, a saved
template, or a GitHub `<owner>/<repo>`.

Headings are the selectable units: selecting one maps the document
section beneath it to a question. Each question then gets validation
rules (counts of chunks, markdown blocks, or other node types; content
checks; name checks), along with optional filters that narrow which
nodes the rules see. Point values are not part of the template; each
question’s total is set with its rubric while grading.

![The template app: document structure tree on the left, questions with
their selected sections and validation rules on the
right](reference/figures/template_screenshot.png)

The template app: document structure tree on the left, questions with
their selected sections and validation rules on the right

When the app is opened on an initialized project, saving writes the
template directly into the project database, ready for grading.

### Whole-document questions

Some problems belong to no single question: a render setting in the YAML
header, global chunk options, a document that does not render. Choosing
“The entire document” in the “Add Question” dialog creates a document
entry for them. It selects no sections (its filters and rules, if any,
run against the whole document) and is written as `scope: document` in
the template YAML (format 3.1).

Add one only when a submission needs it. Paired with rubric scoring that
is worth 0 points, marked optional, and not bounded below zero, it
records such a problem once as a deduction from the total instead of
spreading it across the questions it affects.

### Questions on other files

An assignment can consist of more than the document: scripts students
write, data, images. The Files button in the Questions card’s title bar
picks which of the key directory’s files questions can cover. Hidden
files, render output, lock files, project files, and the README are left
out unless “Show hidden and filtered files” is on.

“Add Question” opens a dialog asking for the question’s name, its file
(the document or one of those files) and, on the document, whether it
covers selected sections or the entire document. The file and coverage
are fixed once the question is added, and are shown beside its name.
Selecting a question on another file shows that file’s source in place
of the document tree.

A question on another file covers the whole file:

- It has no rules.
- While grading it,
  [`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md) shows
  the file from each repository, found by its repository-relative path
  or, failing that, as a file with the same name elsewhere in the
  repository.
- Validation fails a repository that lacks the file.

Templates with files are written as format 3.2, with a top-level
`files:` list and a `file:` field on those questions.

## Grading with `mark()`

[`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md) opens an
initialized project and sources everything from it: the student
repositories, the stored template, the grading database, and each
repository’s rendered reports.

### Assignments

The app opens on the Assignments tab, a single table with one row per
repository. Each row has links to the repository’s folder, GitHub
repository, rendered report, and source, followed by its validation
status, its grading progress, and its score per question and in total.

Scores are computed from the rubric selections with the same code as
[`export_scores()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_scores.md).
Like the export, the total counts only once every question is graded.
Until then the table shows the running sum of the graded questions in
grey, while `scores.csv` leaves `total` empty.

The class summary is pinned beneath the rows: how many repositories are
graded, then the mean, median, and standard deviation per question and
for the total. The table filters by name and by status (failed
validation, incomplete, complete), sorts by any column, and updates as
grading proceeds. Clicking a repository’s validation marker opens its
validation results, and clicking a score opens that repository and
question in the Grade tab.

![The mark app’s Assignments tab: one row per repository with folder,
GitHub, report and source links, validation status, grading progress and
per-question scores, with the class summary pinned
beneath](reference/figures/mark_assignments_screenshot.png)

The mark app’s Assignments tab: one row per repository with folder,
GitHub, report and source links, validation status, grading progress and
per-question scores, with the class summary pinned beneath

### Validation

Validation checks each repository against the template’s rules, so
structural problems (missing sections, missing chunks, absent content)
are visible before any grading starts. The table’s validation column
shows how many questions each repository passed, and clicking it opens
that repository’s per-question results in a modal.

Each question’s card shows its pass or fail mark and its rule results in
the header, with the matched document content collapsed beneath; a
question that is expanded stays expanded for the next repository opened.
The question selector in the modal’s header, whose entries carry each
question’s pass or fail mark, jumps to a question’s results. A content
node’s preview button shows the node’s source, with a Back button to
return to the results.

![The validation modal for one repository: a card per question with its
pass or fail mark and rule results, and the matched content collapsed
beneath](reference/figures/mark_validation_screenshot.png)

The validation modal for one repository: a card per question with its
pass or fail mark and rule results, and the matched content collapsed
beneath

### Grade

The Grade tab is where grading happens. The left pane shows the
student’s rendered report or source, and the right pane shows the
current question’s rubric.

- Items toggle by click or by number key. The first ten items of a
  question get the keys 1-9 and 0; there is no limit on the number of
  items, and those beyond the tenth toggle by click.
- The score follows from the question’s scoring setup: additive or
  deduction mode, with optional clamping between zero and the question
  total. Clicking the score display edits the total, and the gear
  popover holds the mode and bounds.
- Items that stack can be placed in a named group with a floor or
  ceiling on their combined points, so every defect is recorded while
  the deductions stay proportionate. A group can instead be made
  exclusive, so only one severity tier can be selected. A group’s header
  shows its live subtotal and flags a bound that was hit, and a badge
  beside the score opens the breakdown.
- Below the items are two comment boxes: a public, student-facing
  comment (which also marks the question as graded) and private notes
  that are never shared with students.

Every action autosaves to the project database.

![The mark app’s Grade tab: rendered report on the left; rubric items
with hotkeys, an item group, the computed score, and the public and
private comment boxes on the
right](reference/figures/mark_rubric_screenshot.png)

The mark app’s Grade tab: rendered report on the left; rubric items with
hotkeys, an item group, the computed score, and the public and private
comment boxes on the right

Rubric items can be added, edited, reordered, and grouped while grading.
Add Group creates a group whose settings popover holds its label,
bounds, and exclusivity, and each item’s group menu moves it in or out.
The rubric pane’s menu offers YAML import and export for editing the
rubric outside the app.

### Rubric

The Rubric tab shows every question’s rubric in one place, without the
documents. For each question it has the scoring settings (total points,
positive or negative grading, and the optional score bounds) and the
items and groups, all editable as in the Grade tab: descriptions and
points, adding, deleting, reordering, grouping, and group settings. In
place of its toggle, each item shows how many repositories have it
selected. Both tabs edit the same rubric, so a change made in one
appears in the other.

### History

The History tab is a single timeline of the project’s snapshots and its
activity log. A filter narrows the timeline to snapshots, to agents and
scripts, or to grading in the app.

Snapshots are named, timestamped copies of the grading state (template,
rubric, and marks) kept inside the project database. They are taken
automatically before every bulk change (a rubric import, deleting an
item that has selections, deleting a group, a restore), and by hand from
the camera button or the `s` key, with a label and a summary of what is
about to change.

The activity log records every call of a markermd function that changed
the grading state (an import,
[`marks_set()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/marks_set.md),
a restore), alongside the grading done in the app, which is grouped into
sessions. Each entry has its summary, what it touched, and who made it:
`claude` or `codex` when an agent CLI ran it, `R` otherwise, or whatever
`MARKERMD_ACTOR` names. The same log is available from R with
[`project_activity()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/project_activity.md)
and
[`activity_detail()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/activity_detail.md).

Selecting a snapshot shows:

- its fields and notes;
- what changed between it and the current state, or any other snapshot:
  items added, removed, reworded, or re-pointed, selections and comments
  changed, and every repository’s total before and after;
- the scores it recorded.

From there a snapshot can be restored (undoing every change since to the
rubric and marks, or only to chosen questions and repositories),
exported to YAML files, pinned, or deleted, and the database file can be
backed up.

Selecting an activity entry shows what it changed: the items selected
and deselected and the comments and private notes written, per
repository and question, plus the rubric or template changes of a call
that replaced them. A button selects the snapshot taken just before the
entry.

The navbar shows how many selections have been recorded since the latest
snapshot and when that snapshot was taken. It turns amber when the
number grows large, as a nudge to take a named checkpoint at the end of
a session.

### Changes made outside the app

While [`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md)
runs, it notices changes made from outside (an agent in a terminal, a
script) within about a second:

- The Assignments table and History refresh.
- The repository and question on screen are re-read, keeping an unsaved
  comment edit.
- Items an agent selected carry a small robot badge until that
  repository and question are changed in the app.

A changed rubric asks for a page reload, and a changed template for a
restart of
[`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md).

### Terminal

`mark(project, terminal = TRUE)` adds a Terminal tab, using the optional
[shinyterm](https://github.com/rundel/shinyterm) package. Its “+” menu
opens a shell, Claude Code, or Codex in the project root, each agent in
its own sandbox confined to the project. The app is then protected by an
access token in its URL. A terminal runs as you, so this is for your own
machine only.

## Scripting the workflow

Everything the apps do is also available headlessly:

| Task | Functions |
|----|----|
| Check submissions | [`validate_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/validate_project.md), [`parse_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/parse_project.md), [`scan_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/scan_project.md) |
| Move the template to and from YAML | [`template_import()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template_import.md), [`template_export()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template_export.md) |
| Move the rubric to and from YAML, edit items | [`rubric_import()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/rubric_import.md), [`rubric_export()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/rubric_export.md), [`rubric_item_set()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/rubric_item_set.md) |
| Move marks to and from YAML, set one pair | [`marks_import()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/marks_import.md), [`marks_export()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/marks_export.md), [`marks_set()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/marks_set.md) |
| Write scores and feedback | [`export_feedback()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_feedback.md), [`export_scores()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_scores.md), [`export_comments()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_comments.md) |

``` r

# Check every student repository against the stored template
validate_project("hw01")

# Templates, rubrics, and recorded marks round trip between the
# project database and editable YAML files
template_export("hw01-template.yaml", project = "hw01")
rubric_import("hw01-rubric.yaml", project = "hw01")
marks_export("hw01-marks.yaml", project = "hw01")

# Record marks for a single repository/question pair
marks_set("student1-hw01", "Question 2",
  items = "Looks good",
  private_comment = "Quartiles and summary statistics all present.",
  project = "hw01"
)
```

The YAML formats are validated against bundled JSON Schemas (see
`system.file("schema", package = "markermd")`) and are deliberately
simple enough for LLM tools to author. Marks imports are conservative by
default: repository/question pairs that already have grading activity
are skipped unless explicitly overwritten.

### Snapshots

Every bulk change to the grading state takes a snapshot of the state it
replaces, in the same transaction, so a change cannot succeed without
its snapshot. The imports take a `summary` argument, so the reason for a
change is recorded with it.

Snapshots can be listed, compared, exported, and restored from R as well
as from the History tab of
[`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md). The
template editor also has controls for taking a snapshot and for loading
a snapshot’s template.

``` r

# A named checkpoint before a multi-step change
snapshot_create("hw01", label = "Before feedback review",
  summary = "Re-checking every Q1 selection against the reviewed standard.")

# Imports record their reason on the snapshot they take
rubric_import("hw01-rubric.yaml", project = "hw01", mode = "replace",
  summary = "Feedback review: lenient Q1a standard, unrequested items to 0 pts")

# What changed since, and what it did to the grades
snapshot_list("hw01")
snapshot_diff("Before feedback review", project = "hw01")

# Undo (the state before the restore is snapshotted first)
snapshot_restore("Before feedback review", project = "hw01",
  summary = "The review's Q1c severities were wrong.")

# An archive of one snapshot as YAML files, and a copy of the database file
snapshot_export("Before feedback review", "backups/before-review", project = "hw01")
project_backup("hw01")
```

Snapshots live in the project database; an existing database from before
they were added gains a baseline snapshot when first opened. A few
details keep them cheap and traceable:

- Identical parts are stored once.
- An automatic snapshot of an unchanged state is recorded as a note on
  the latest snapshot rather than as a new one.
- [`snapshot_prune()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_prune.md)
  removes old automatic snapshots while keeping every manual or pinned
  one.
- [`export_scores()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_scores.md)
  and
  [`export_comments()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_comments.md)
  record which snapshot each export came from.
- [`project_sitrep()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/project_sitrep.md)
  reports the snapshot state, including whether the exported scores are
  stale.

## Exporting results

When grading is complete,
[`export_feedback()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_feedback.md)
writes the final hand-off files from the project database. It runs
[`export_scores()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_scores.md)
and
[`export_comments()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_comments.md),
which can also be called individually:

``` r

export_feedback("hw01")
```

### Scores

[`export_scores()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_scores.md)
writes `scores.csv` to the project root: one row per repository, one
column per question, plus a `total` column.

- Scores are recomputed exactly as
  [`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md)
  displays them: each item group’s combined points are clamped to its
  floor and ceiling, then the question’s selected item points pass
  through its grading mode and bounds.
- Ungraded repository/question pairs export as `NA`, and a repository’s
  total stays `NA` until all of its questions are graded.
- A question whose scoring is marked optional counts as graded for every
  repository, scoring as if no item were selected until something is
  recorded. The option is “Optional: nothing selected still counts as
  graded” in the gear popover, or `optional: true` in the rubric YAML,
  and the question’s column in the Assignments table has a small red dot
  beside its name.

### Comments

[`export_comments()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_comments.md)
writes each repository’s student-facing feedback to
`comments/<repo>.md`, or to the project’s configured comments directory.

- Each graded question appears as a heading, in template order
  (document-scope questions first), followed by a bulleted list of its
  selected rubric item descriptions and its public comment.
- Group bounds are never mentioned. With `group_headings = TRUE`, a
  group’s selected items are listed under a subheading carrying its
  label.
- Private notes are never exported, and a repository with no public
  feedback gets no file.

## Agent skills (Claude Code and Codex)

[`init_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/init_project.md)
installs five agent skills into the project, in two sets: a [Claude
Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) set under `.claude/skills/` and a
[Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex) set under
`.agents/skills/`. The `agents` argument selects one or both, and the
default installs both. Both sets follow the Agent Skills format and
share the same names, so a skill is invoked as `/markermd-fix-parsing`
in Claude Code and `$markermd-fix-parsing` in Codex.

- `markermd-scaffold-template` builds a starter grading template from
  the key repository’s assignment document.
- `markermd-fix-parsing` repairs student documents that the strict q2r
  parser rejects. It makes the smallest possible edits on a
  `grading-fixes` branch in each repository, so the original submission
  stays intact, and flags any substantive change in the document.
- `markermd-check-injection` scans every student repository and rendered
  report for prompt injection attempts: hidden or visible text aimed at
  an automated grader, found by the deterministic
  [`scan_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/scan_project.md).
  It triages the candidates and reports the evidence for the instructor,
  and never edits a repository or changes marks.
- `markermd-scaffold-rubric` drafts per-question rubric items and
  scoring from the key, optionally sampling student submissions to
  anticipate common mistakes.
- `markermd-apply-rubric` applies the stored rubric to every student
  repository as a first-pass machine grading, recording its reasoning as
  private notes for human review in
  [`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md).

[`init_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/init_project.md)
also writes a project instructions file for each selected agent at the
project root: `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code and `AGENTS.md` for Codex. The
file describes:

- the project layout, the workflow, and the skills;
- the headless entry points;
- the template, rubric, and marks YAML formats;
- the rules for working with student submissions and for keeping the
  project root clean (working files go under `scratch/`, notes worth
  keeping under `notes/`).

An existing instructions file is kept, so it can be customized per
project. `overwrite_instructions = TRUE` replaces it with the packaged
version (to pick up a newer markermd’s instructions), and
`instructions = FALSE` skips the step.

See `inst/skills/README.md` for details and per-user installation.

## Contributing

markermd is in active development. Contributions, bug reports, and
feature requests are welcome!

GPL (\>= 3)

# Package index

## Project setup and management

Initialize a grading project and inspect or edit its configuration.

- [`init_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/init_project.md)
  : Initialize a markermd grading project
- [`project_config()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/project_config.md)
  : Read a markermd project's configuration
- [`project_set()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/project_set.md)
  : Change a markermd project's configuration
- [`project_sitrep()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/project_sitrep.md)
  : Report a markermd project's status
- [`validate_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/validate_project.md)
  : Validate a project's student repositories against its template
- [`parse_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/parse_project.md)
  : Check that every student repository's assignment document parses
- [`scan_project()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/scan_project.md)
  : Scan a project's submissions for prompt injection attempts
- [`markermd_skills_path()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/markermd_skills_path.md)
  : Path to the bundled markermd agent skills

## Grading apps

The interactive template editor and marking interface.

- [`mark()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/mark.md) :
  Launch the markermd Marking Application
- [`template()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template.md)
  : Launch the markermd Template Creation Application

## Templates

Author, inspect, and move grading templates in and out of the project
database.

- [`assignment_outline()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/assignment_outline.md)
  : Outline the gradable sections of an assignment
- [`template_import()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template_import.md)
  : Import a grading template from YAML into a project's database
- [`template_export()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template_export.md)
  : Export a project's grading template to YAML
- [`template_add_question()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template_add_question.md)
  : Add a question to a template
- [`template_remove_question()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template_remove_question.md)
  : Remove a question from a template
- [`template_question()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template_question.md)
  : Get a template's question by ID
- [`template_methods`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/template_methods.md)
  : Methods for Markermd Template Classes
- [`parse_assignment_document()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/parse_assignment_document.md)
  : Parse an assignment document into a Pandoc AST

## Rubrics

Move per-question rubrics between the project database and YAML.

- [`rubric_import()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/rubric_import.md)
  : Import a grading rubric from YAML into a project's database
- [`rubric_export()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/rubric_export.md)
  : Export a project's grading rubric to YAML
- [`rubric_item_set()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/rubric_item_set.md)
  : Reword or re-point one rubric item

## Marks and score export

Import, export, and set recorded grading, and export scores and
comments.

- [`marks_import()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/marks_import.md)
  : Import grading marks from YAML into a project's database
- [`marks_export()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/marks_export.md)
  : Export a project's grading marks to YAML
- [`marks_set()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/marks_set.md)
  : Record grading marks for one repository/question pair
- [`export_scores()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_scores.md)
  : Export per-repository scores to a CSV file
- [`export_comments()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_comments.md)
  : Export student-facing feedback to per-repository markdown files
- [`export_feedback()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/export_feedback.md)
  : Export scores and feedback for a graded project

## Snapshots

Named, annotated copies of the grading state kept in the project
database, and how to compare and restore them.

- [`snapshot_create()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_create.md)
  : Take a snapshot of a project's grading state
- [`snapshot_list()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_list.md)
  : List a project's snapshots
- [`snapshot_info()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_info.md)
  : Inspect one snapshot
- [`snapshot_annotate()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_annotate.md)
  : Annotate a snapshot
- [`snapshot_diff()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_diff.md)
  : Compare two snapshots, or a snapshot with the live state
- [`snapshot_scores()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_scores.md)
  : Scores recorded in a snapshot, or the live scores
- [`snapshot_restore()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_restore.md)
  : Restore a snapshot's grading state
- [`snapshot_export()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_export.md)
  : Export a snapshot to YAML files
- [`snapshot_pin()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_pin.md)
  : Pin or unpin a snapshot
- [`snapshot_delete()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_delete.md)
  : Delete a snapshot
- [`snapshot_prune()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/snapshot_prune.md)
  : Prune old automatic snapshots
- [`project_backup()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/project_backup.md)
  : Back up the project database file
- [`markermd_snapshot()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/markermd_snapshot.md)
  : Snapshot of a project's grading state
- [`markermd_snapshot_diff()`](https://rundel.github.io/markermd/reference/markermd_snapshot_diff.md)
  : Differences between two snapshots

## Activity log

Read the recorded changes to a project’s grading state.

  : Validate a template file against the markermd JSON Schema

  : Write a grading rubric to a YAML file

  : Validate a rubric file against the markermd JSON Schema
